title: First-level Fourier weight of an upper-tail indicator
statement: For each real $t$, take the indicator on the sign cube of dimension $m+1$ that equals $1$ when the normalized sum of its coordinates exceeds $t$, and $0$ otherwise. As $m$ tends to infinity, the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of this indicator over all singleton coordinate sets tends to the square of the standard Gaussian density at $t$.
